label: 2027 Budget Priorities Framework: macroeconomic and fiscal environment (DBM)
title: Briefer on the 2027 Budget Priorities Framework (Macroeconomic and Fiscal Environment), Department of Budget and Management

sections.heading: Proposed FY 2027 budget
sections.text: At a record high of Php 7.2 trillion, or 21.7% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), the proposed FY 2027 National Budget is guided by the theme "People-Centered Growth for an Inclusive and Resilient Future." This fiscal plan prioritizes the prudent and strategic allocation of resources, ensuring that every peso is spent with a continued commitment to fiscal responsibility while advancing the goal of a more resilient and secure future for all Filipinos.

sections.heading: Inflation
sections.text: Inflation is projected to average 6.0%–7.0% in 2026, reflecting higher commodity prices and temporary supply-side pressures associated with the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Inflation is expected to gradually ease thereafter as global conditions stabilize. Macroeconomic assumptions: inflation rate 1.7% (2025 actual), 6.0–7.0% (2026), 4.0–5.0% (2027), 2.0–4.0% (2028 to 2030).

sections.heading: Fiscal program
sections.text: Amid evolving macroeconomic conditions and geopolitical events that continue to reshape the country's growth and fiscal outlook, the Administration has recalibrated its medium-term fiscal strategy to provide additional support for economic growth while remaining firmly committed to fiscal consolidation over the medium term.

sections.heading: Deficit
sections.text: The fiscal deficit is projected to gradually narrow from 5.4% of GDP in 2026 to 3.5% by 2030, consistent with the government's medium-term fiscal consolidation strategy following temporary adjustments to cushion the economy against external shocks.

sections.heading: Revenues and disbursements
sections.text: On average, revenue collections are projected to grow by nearly 8.0% annually from FYs 2026 to 2030. This growth is expected to sustain revenues at around 16.0% of GDP for the same period, driven by ongoing digitalization initiatives and strengthened tax administration and enforcement measures. Disbursements are programmed to reach 21.2% of GDP in 2026, then gradually decline to 19.1% by 2030, consistent with fiscal consolidation.
